paper_metadata.title: Quantum alternating operator ansatz with PSO optimizer for portfolio optimization problem

summary: The paper proposes PSO-QAOAz for portfolio optimization in two variants: risk parity (RP) and mean-variance (MV), both using a 5-layer QAOAz circuit with a ring XY-mixer and PSO tuning over 10 iterations. On six-asset portfolios, PSO-QAOAz-RP achieves best AR values up to 100.00% on some portfolios and 92.88% on Portfolio 1, while PSO-QAOAz-MV reaches 100% AR on several Chinese portfolios; however, classical baselines still outperform on some RP cases (notably portfolios 7-8), and no real quantum hardware advantage is shown.

experiments.description: QAOAz-RP portfolio optimization on six-asset portfolios from Chinese, U.S., European, and emerging markets, compared against GA, ABC-LP, and GWO baselines.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz (QAOAz) for risk parity (RP) with ring XY-mixer and PSO-optimized parameters
algorithm.ansatz: QAOAz circuit with alternating problem unitary and ring XY-mixer unitary
algorithm.convergence_criteria: PSO run for 10 iterations; QAOAz depth fixed at p=5
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Parameters initialized in [0, 2π]; PSO particles initialized with positions and velocities

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary selection variables x_i indicate whether each asset is included; six assets per portfolio; cardinality constraint enforced with fixed B
problem_formulation.objective_function: F_RP = sum_{i=1}^n sum_{j=1}^n (x_i(ΣX)_i - x_j(ΣX)_j)^2 + A(∑_{i=1}^n x_i - B)^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Cardinality constraint removed from problem Hamiltonian and incorporated into the mixer via XY-mixer; penalty term A(∑x_i-B)^2 appears in the classical objective formulation
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_p derived from RP objective with Z_i, Z_i Z_j, Z_i Z_j Z_k, and Z_i Z_j Z_k Z_l terms; quartic terms implemented directly via parity-check method

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization under the risk parity model on 12 portfolios, each with 6 assets; experiments reported for portfolios 1–8 in the main tables, with 1–6 used for RP and 7–8 also included in RP evaluation
problem_instance.dataset_name: Multiple market portfolios (Chinese A-shares, U.S. stocks, European stocks, emerging markets)

dataset_specification.description: Portfolios 1–6: Chinese A-share CSI-300 constituents; Portfolios 7–8: U.S. stocks (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA, META; TSLA, JPM, BRK-B, V, JNJ, UNH); Portfolios 9–10: European stocks; Portfolios 11–12: emerging markets; date range 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Covariance matrices computed from 2022 market data; six stocks selected per portfolio; no further preprocessing details reported
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each algorithm run 10 times; best, worst, average, standard deviation, and approximate ratio reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Covariance matrices and expected returns computed from historical market data; portfolio selection constrained to six assets
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measured bitstrings converted to portfolio weights; objective function and approximate ratio computed from sampled solutions

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: convergence evaluated over PSO iterations; stable by 10 iterations

results.uncertainty: best reported value; exact table entry
worst reported value; exact table entry
average over 10 runs; exact table entry

speedup_claims.conditions: Empirical comparison on six-asset portfolios; no asymptotic or wall-clock speedup reported
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports better optimization quality and lower standard deviation, but not runtime speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Ring XY-mixer can be implemented in depth O(log n) on an all-to-all qubit device; complete graph mixer query complexity O(n^2/sqrt(δ)) with error δ

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No quantum hardware demonstrated; Cirq-based implementation with PSO classical outer loop and 6-asset instances
limiting_factors: Classical baselines outperform on some portfolios (notably portfolios 7-8)
No end-to-end speedup or crossover analysis reported

notes: num_qubits inferred as 6 logical qubits from six binary asset-selection variables per portfolio; the paper does not explicitly state the register size.
hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports Cirq-based experiments but no real QPU or noisy simulator device.
The paper reports ring XY-mixer depth O(log n) and complete-graph mixer query complexity, but does not claim an asymptotic end-to-end speedup over classical methods.
Authors report QAOAz-RP beats GA/ABC-LP/GWO on many portfolios, but also state it underperforms classical methods on portfolios 7-8.
No practical quantum advantage is demonstrated.
